title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 74 (Repayment of pre-Act deposits)

content.overview: For deposits accepted before commencement of the Companies Act, 2013 that remained unpaid or became due, the company must file a statement of unpaid deposits/interest and repayment arrangements within three months of commencement or when payment becomes due, and repay within three years of commencement or by the original deposit term's expiry, whichever is earlier. The Tribunal may allow further time on application.

The Tribunal may allow further time on application.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 74 (Repayment of deposits accepted before commencement). For a deposit accepted before commencement of the 2013 Act where the amount, part or interest remained unpaid at commencement or became due later, the company must file with the Registrar, within three months of commencement or the date payment becomes due, a statement of deposits and sums remaining unpaid, interest and repayment arrangements. Under the amendment effective 15 August 2018, repayment is due within three years from commencement or on/before expiry of the period for which the deposit was accepted, whichever is earlier; renewal must comply with Chapter V and the rules. On application, the Tribunal may allow further time after considering the company's financial condition, amount and interest, and other relevant matters. If the company fails to repay within the applicable period or Tribunal extension, it must repay the amount and interest and is punishable with a fine of at least ₹1 crore up to ₹10 crore; every officer in default is punishable with imprisonment up to seven years, or a fine of at least ₹25 lakh up to ₹2 crore, or both. Section 75 separately addresses personal damages liability where fraudulent intent/purpose is proved. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Scope and Registrar statement
sections.body: Section 74 concerns deposits accepted before commencement of the Companies Act, 2013 where the deposit, part or interest remained unpaid at commencement or became due thereafter. The company must file with the Registrar, within three months of commencement or the date the payment becomes due, a statement of all such deposits, sums unpaid, interest payable and repayment arrangements.

sections.heading: Repayment deadline
sections.body: As amended with effect from 15 August 2018, the company must repay within three years from commencement or on/before expiry of the period for which the deposits were accepted, whichever is earlier. Renewal of such deposits must comply with Chapter V and the rules.

sections.heading: Tribunal extension
sections.body: On the company's application, the Tribunal may allow further time considered reasonable after considering the company's financial condition, amount of deposit/part and interest payable, and other relevant matters.

sections.heading: Failure to repay: company penalty
sections.body: If the company fails to repay within the applicable period or Tribunal-allowed extension, it remains liable to repay the deposit/part and interest and is punishable with a fine of at least ₹1 crore and up to ₹10 crore.

sections.heading: Failure to repay: officer consequences
sections.body: Every officer of the company in default is punishable with imprisonment up to seven years, or a fine of at least ₹25 lakh and up to ₹2 crore, or both.

sections.heading: Separate fraud-damages route
sections.body: Section 75 separately imposes personal liability for depositor losses/damages on officers responsible for accepting deposits where the relevant non-repayment and fraudulent-intent/purpose requirements are proved.

hypotheticals.question: A deposit accepted before commencement of the 2013 Act remains unpaid. What filing and repayment timeframes apply under the amended section 74?
hypotheticals.analysis: The company must file the statement of unpaid deposits/interest and repayment arrangements within three months of commencement or when payment becomes due. Repayment is due within three years from commencement or by expiry of the original deposit term, whichever is earlier, subject to any further time allowed by the Tribunal.

hypotheticals.question: The company fails to repay within the applicable period or Tribunal extension. What penalties apply under section 74(3)?
hypotheticals.analysis: The company must repay the deposit/part and interest and is punishable with a fine of at least ₹1 crore up to ₹10 crore. Every officer in default faces imprisonment up to seven years, or a fine of at least ₹25 lakh up to ₹2 crore, or both.

misconceptions.trap: Using the original one-year repayment period instead of the amended three-year rule.
misconceptions.correction: The 2017 amendment, effective 15 August 2018, substituted a three-year period from commencement or expiry of the original deposit term, whichever is earlier.

misconceptions.trap: Treating the Tribunal's extension as automatic.
misconceptions.correction: The company must apply and the Tribunal considers financial condition, deposit/interest amounts and other relevant matters.

misconceptions.trap: Omitting the severe separate consequences for the company and officers in default.
misconceptions.correction: Subsection (3) specifies the company fine and the officer's imprisonment/fine alternatives.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 74 require?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Deposits accepted before the Act had to be repaid within the statutory window, failing which the Tribunal may order repayment with the consequences in the section.
